what_this_is: The two hand-written inputs the FLOW-INTEGRITY doctrine needs. Everything else it checks is re-derived from the repository on every run. These are here because they are human DECISIONS that nothing can re-derive: which workflows were MEASURED not to need generated parsers, and which hand-off consumers do not yet verify the artifacts they are handed.
single_source_note: ci_workflow_local_gate.sh's audit_workflow_regeneration_surface reads regeneration_exempt_workflows from THIS FILE rather than keeping its own copy. Two lists that must agree are two lists that can disagree — CI-PARITY-GATE-ROT.1 found twelve assertions rotted exactly that way.

regeneration_exempt_workflows._why: MEASURED to PASS against a tracked-files-only tree (the shape actions/checkout yields) with no generated/ present. Evidence: CI-PARITY-GATE-ROT.3's unprepared census. Exemption is asserted in BOTH directions: an exempt workflow that ACQUIRES the step also fails, because a 236s regeneration bolted onto a 1s shell check is a cost regression.

handoff_provenance_ratchet._why: A gate that accepts EXISTING_*_STATE_DIR is told 'this artifact exists, do not produce it'. Taking that on trust let a sota_exit_gate run consume a THREE-DAY-OLD artifact as current proof (CI-PARITY-GATE-ROT.7). require_supplied_state_dir makes the hand-off prove its provenance instead. Coverage at adoption: 1 of 23 consumers.
handoff_provenance_ratchet._rule: This list may only SHRINK. A NEW hand-off consumer that does not verify FAILS the doctrine; an entry that has started verifying must be REMOVED, so the list cannot hold dead exemptions. It is deliberately NOT a bare count: a count lets one gate regress while another improves.
